phase_0.domain_name: Erdős distinct subset sum problem space
phase_0.boundary_condition: The Erdős condition: for a set of n integers, all 2^n subset sums are pairwise distinct.

VINIT.chosen_element: empty set and empty sum set
VINIT.justification: Before any elements are chosen, no set exists and no subset sums are defined — the void state prior to genesis of the candidate.

TANCH.chosen_element: declaration that the constructed set must satisfy the Erdős property
TANCH.justification: Acts as the terminal anchor that seals the candidate once construction is complete; it closes the system by asserting the global constraint.

AFWD.chosen_element: addition of a new element to the set and computation of the resulting subset sums
AFWD.justification: Forward morphism that extends the current set by a chosen integer and propagates the sum set forward by adding the new element to every existing sum.

AREV.justification: Reverse transformation used to retract a candidate element if its addition introduces a duplicate subset sum; returns the system to the state prior to the attempt.

CLINK.justification: Chains the steps of construction so that the output of one element addition becomes the input to the next.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: self-identity of the sum set as a set of integers
IMSCRIB.justification: Each subset sum is simply itself; the sum set recognizes no internal structure beyond membership, establishing the identity morphism.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: partition of the full sum set into lower half (sums not containing the largest element) and upper half (sums containing it)
FSPLIT.justification: Co-multiplication branches the complete sum set into two disjoint sum families determined by the presence of the most significant power of two; this split leverages the binary structure inherent in a valid Erdős set.

FFUSE.chosen_element: reunion of the two sum family halves
FFUSE.justification: Multiplication that merges the lower and upper sum families to recover the exact original full sum set; guarantees FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation when the two halves are disjoint — the size of the union equals twice the size of each half, confirming no duplicate sums.

EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation when an overlap exists between the lower and upper sum families, indicating that the set does not have the Erdős property.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: a sum that simultaneously belongs to both the lower and upper families
ENGAGR.justification: Paradice: a single integer appears as a subset sum both with and without the largest element, held in an unresolved paradoxical state.

IFIX.chosen_element: committing a chosen element to the permanent set, and later recording the verification result
IFIX.justification: Irreversible fixation; once an element satisfies the distinctness condition it becomes a permanent part of the Erdős set, and the final verification is recorded as immutable truth.

split_outputs: sums of subsets that do not contain the largest element (values less than 2^(n-1))
sums of subsets that contain the largest element (values at least 2^(n-1))
phase_2.fuse_element: set union of the two sum halves

phase_3.void_description: no set exists; no sums computed.
phase_3.true_description: the subset sum set has size exactly 2^n, with every sum unique — Erdős property holds.
phase_3.false_description: a duplicate subset sum exists; the candidate fails the Erdős condition.
phase_3.both_description: a specific sum value appears in both the lower and upper families, constituting a collision that is simultaneously true and false — a paradice.
